links.comparator_used: Raw ASR output (baseline gpt-4o-transcribe transcripts without postprocessing)
links.outcome: Character error rate and BERTScore versus original written notes
links.effect: Baseline BERTScore 0.9131 and CER 0.2336. LLM-only postprocessing reduced CER by 36.09% (Claude Sonnet 4) and 32.53% (GPT-4o). Dictionary+LLM with Claude Sonnet 4 reached BERTScore 0.9638 and CER 0.0820, a 64.9% CER reduction from baseline (P<.001).
links.quote: The combined dictionary-LLM approach achieved the best performance: Claude Sonnet 4 attained a BERTScore of 0.9638 and CER of 0.0820, representing a 64.9% reduction in CER from baseline (P<.001).

links.comparator_used: Different temperature settings (0.0-0.8) across six LLMs
links.outcome: Postprocessing performance (BERTScore, CER) across temperature settings
links.effect: All models had small temperature-related effect sizes (all |Cohen dz| ≤0.15); GPT-4o showed the largest dependency, with significant improvement at temperature 0.6 (Holm-adjusted P<.001 for BERTScore and CER); the 4 Claude variants and GPT-4.1 performed practically consistently across all settings.
links.quote: Temperature optimization showed that all postprocessing models had small temperature-related effect sizes (all |Cohen dz| ≤0.15), with GPT-4o exhibiting the largest dependency and statistically significant improvement at temperature 0.6 (Holm-adjusted P<.001 for both BERTScore and CER) and the 4 Claude variants and GPT-4.1 exhibiting practically consistent performance across all settings.

design_hint: dictionary normalization plus LLM postprocessing of ASR output
